title: Escape every bare interpolation in an HTML fragment template literal

facts.note: Server-rendered fragments are template literals in TS/JS source on a Bun + htmx workspace (atdd.workspace.bun).
Test files (*.test.*, *.spec.*) are excluded by the source.

values: html_bearing_template literal added or edited containing a bare_interpolation
facts.note: Diff-level fact for the coder; needs a brace-depth-aware template-literal extractor that keeps literals containing an opening tag and classifies interpolation expressions. The detector itself still scans every HTML-bearing literal in non-test source, not only changed ones.

values: htmx_hypermedia_detector: bare interpolation in HTML-bearing template
facts.note: Detector finding from the htmx_hypermedia_detector family implementation.
Contextual hint only, not an independent sufficient trigger; the rule fires on the code shape.

fires:
A server handler returns a backtick template literal containing `
  • ${order.title}
    • ` that htmx swaps into the DOM.
A fragment helper interpolates `${title}` or `${user.name}` directly between or inside tags.
An edit adds a new property-chain interpolation (`${order.customer.name}`) to an existing markup template literal.
doesNotFire: A template literal with no opening tag (log line, SQL string, URL).
An interpolation that is a call, e.g. `${escapeHtml(x)}` or `${rows.map(row).join("")}` (detector-wise; review still applies to non-escaping calls).

given: Server code builds an HTML fragment as a template literal containing an opening tag; htmx inserts it via innerHTML with no auto-escaping in the path
when: a value is interpolated into that markup
then: Never interpolate a bare identifier or property chain (`${user.name}`) into the markup; route the value through an escaping helper at the interpolation site.
prefer: Escape at the RENDER site, where the destination is known, so it is escaped exactly once.
Nest fragments via calls whose inner fragments escape their own data.
avoid: Escaping at storage/fetch: double-escaped when it reaches a non-HTML sink.
A call that neither escapes nor nests (`${format(bio)}`): passes the detector, still a violation; review catches it.
The JSX habit of bare interpolation, assuming escaping happens underneath.
unless: The literal has no opening tag (not markup; never scanned).
The interpolation is a call, treated as escaping or composition (detector scope; non-escaping calls remain a review concern).
why: Escaping is implicit in JSX (`{value}` auto-escaped) but explicit here; carrying over bare interpolation without the invisible escaping yields stored XSS in code that looks like what teams wrote before.
evidence: htmx_hypermedia_detector reports zero bare_interpolation findings in HTML-bearing template literals of non-test files.
No interpolation in an HTML-bearing literal is a bare identifier or property chain; operator and literal expressions are outside this rule's scope.
Reviewer checks call interpolations that neither escape nor nest (e.g. `${format(bio)}`), since the detector passes them.
Values are escaped at the render site, not at storage/fetch (no double-escaping in non-HTML sinks).
verifier_detail: html_bearing_template: a backtick template literal whose text contains an opening tag (`<div`, `<li …`); that is the signal it is markup rather than a log line or SQL string. Literals without an opening tag are never scanned.
bare_interpolation: expression is only an identifier or property chain — `${title}`, `${order.customer.name}`; no call, no operator, no literal. This is raw data reaching markup and is flagged.

composition: an interpolation that is a CALL — `${escapeHtml(x)}`, `${rows.map(row).join("")}` — either an escape helper or fragment nesting; deliberately out of scope because flagging it would bury the rule in false positives on legitimate composition.

Detector: zero-dependency Bun detector; extracts every template literal brace-depth aware (a nested object inside an interpolation does not end the literal early), keeps those containing an opening tag, flags bare identifier/property-chain interpolations.

Deliberately narrow so it is precise rather than noisy: catches the shape that is ALWAYS wrong (raw data dropped straight into markup) and says nothing about calls, which may be escaping helpers or nested fragments. A call that neither escapes nor nests (`${format(bio)}`) passes and must be caught by review; narrowing was the price of a signal a team will not switch off.
Disposition strict, severity 1 — this is the extension's security rule.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic 'untrusted data is escaped at the rendering boundary' obligation, enforced by the htmx_hypermedia_detector family implementation on atdd.workspace.bun.
Summary: a 'fragments escape their data' obligation, and the security-critical rule of the htmx extension.
Original name: HTML fragments escape interpolated values before htmx swaps them into the DOM.
